title: The late-arriving 2023 East China Sea marine heatwave
query: Using the supplied OISST daily sea surface temperature for 1982-2023, GLORYS12 daily temperature and velocity, and ERA5 hourly surface heat-flux components (net shortwave, net longwave, sensible and latent heat) for May-November of 1993-2011 and 2023 over the East China Sea, test the following findings of Oh et al. (2024, npj Climate and Atmospheric Science, doi:10.1038/s41612-024-00846-4): (1) a marine heatwave occurred in the East China Sea from 12 August to 13 October 2023, later than the typical July onset; (2) its early phase was driven by shortwave radiation and ocean dynamics; (3) in its later phase weaker northerly winds let warm, humid southerlies dominate, reducing the air-sea humidity difference and the ocean's latent heat loss, which prolonged the event; (4) CMIP6 projections link such delayed heatwaves to weak air-sea heat exchange. State your marine-heatwave definition and baseline, give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence, and explain differences from the paper.

paper.title: Late-arriving 2023 summer marine heatwave in the East China Sea and implications for global warming

period_match.paper_data: OISST, GLORYS12, ERA5 over 25-34 N, 120-128 E
period_match.supplied_period: OISST 1982-2023 daily; GLORYS12 and ERA5 May-November 1993-2011 and 2023
period_match.note: The paper's heat budget covers 30 June-19 October, inside the supplied May-November months.
